Article Title: ‘Could result in injury or death’: Thanedar urges US to halt ICE’s electric shock glove plan
Article Text:
Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar warns against ICE’s electric shock gloves

Lawmakers warn of potential misuse

What are the electric shock gloves?

Concerns over ICE's use of force

Indian-American Congressman Shri Thanedar and two other senior Democratic lawmakers have urged the US government to immediately halt Immigration and Customs Enforcement's (ICE) plan to procure gloves capable of delivering electric shocks to officers and agents.In a letter to homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin on Friday, Thanedar, Bennie G Thompson and Lou Correa warned that the devices could be incorrectly used or abused by ICE personnel, potentially resulting "in injury or death".ICE plans to spend up to $20 million to purchase thousands of the devices, described by the Department of Homeland Security as “conductive distraction and de-escalation devices”.The procurement was first announced on August 10, according to a Democratic lawmakers' press release.Thanedar, Thompson and Correa said the devices require significant training and restraint by officers.“Given ICE’s horrific record of violence against the public, the agency must not be allowed to equip its officers and agents with a device that demands both significant training for and restraint by its users,” the lawmakers said in their letter.They also criticised the training of ICE personnel under President Donald Trump.“Under Trump, ICE has hired unqualified officers and agents and rushed them through training programs with reduced use of force instruction. Many of these officers and agents should not have been hired at all, much less let loose on American streets with a badge, a gun, and electric shock gloves,” they said.The three lawmakers urged Mullin to intervene and stop the procurement before it moves forward.Thompson is the ranking member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, while Correa and Thanedar are ranking members of the subcommittees on Border Security and Enforcement, and Oversight, Investigations and Accountability, respectively.ICE's planned procurement involves devices known as the GLOVE, or Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter.The gloves function as normal patrol gloves until an officer activates their electrical mode with a button. The device must be applied directly to a person's skin to deliver a voltage intended to cause pain and gain compliance from someone resisting an officer.Unlike Tasers, the gloves do not leave burns or contact marks, news agency AP reported.The devices are marketed as non-lethal and safe for the heart. However, the manufacturer warns that they “may result in injury or death”, according to the Democratic lawmakers' press release.The manufacturer warns against using the gloves on certain groups, including elderly people, small children, pregnant women and severely handicapped people. Its user manual also warns that the devices should not be used in response to verbal defiance or for punishment, torture or horseplay.ICE's proposed purchase is expected to cover between $10 million and $20 million worth of equipment, with the contract potentially running through March 31, 2027.The lawmakers' demand comes amid criticism of ICE's use of force during Trump's mass deportation campaign.ICE officers have increasingly used force to remove people from vehicles and have faced protests over their actions.Civil rights advocates and Democratic lawmakers have also criticised the planned procurement.Former ICE acting director John Sandweg said the gloves could be misused against people who do not pose a threat.Northern Kentucky University law professor Michael Mannheimer also raised concerns about whether officers could use the devices before considering less forceful options, AP reported.A pending lawsuit alleges a 43-year-old man died in 2024 after being shocked 27 times with the gloves and 13 additional times with a Taser at a jail in Richmond, Kentucky.An internal investigation found that two of the glove shocks lasted 45 and 99 seconds, considerably longer than the manufacturer's recommended 15-second limit.Two other lawsuits also alleged injuries involving the gloves, although both cases were dismissed.The Department of Homeland Security has defended ICE's broader equipment procurement process, saying the agency assesses the needs of officers in the field and reviews technology to ensure it complies with applicable law enforcement policies and standards.
Article Summary: ICE plans to spend up to $20 million to purchase thousands of the devices. The gloves function as normal patrol gloves until an officer activates their electrical mode with a button. The device must be applied directly to a person's skin to deliver a voltage intended to cause pain and gain compliance.

Article Title: Mexican governor seeks leave again amid backlash after return following US drug charges indictment
Article Text:
Mexican governor has been accused of drug trafficking by the US, but Mexico has said there isn't substantial evidence

Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha has again asked to step away from office, just days after returning to his post following a more than three-month leave prompted by US drug-trafficking charges.Rocha, 77, sought the leave on Saturday amid growing political pressure over his return, reported Reuters. His decision to reclaim office had drawn criticism from Mexico’s government and his own Morena party, which accused him of putting personal interests ahead of the public.President Claudia Sheinbaum added to the pressure without naming Rocha directly. In a post on X, she wrote that “power without principles becomes arrogance” and that “no personal interest can ever be above those of the people or the Nation.”Rocha echoed the message in his own X post, saying: “Sinaloa, the nation, and the transformation movement are above all else.”The governor returned on Friday after spending more than three months on leave following US federal charges accusing him and nine other current and former officials of working with a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel known as Los Chapitos.Prosecutors in April alleged that the officials helped the cartel traffic drugs into the United States in return for political support and bribes.The case marked a rare expansion of US anti-cartel action to a senior sitting Mexican politician.Rocha has rejected the allegations, calling the US case a politically motivated attack on Sheinbaum’s movement. Days after the indictment was unsealed in April, he said he would take a “temporary leave of absence” to focus on defending himself.Mexico’s government has also said Washington had not provided enough evidence to justify his arrest or extradition, while opening its own investigation into the allegations.His brief return to office, however, exposed divisions within the ruling party and renewed questions over his political future.
Article Summary: Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha has asked to step away from office. His decision to reclaim office had drawn criticism from Mexico’s government and his own Morena party. He has been accused of working with a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel known as Los Chapitos.

Article Title: ‘Will target their interests’: Iran warns neighbours against supporting US economic pressure tactics
Article Text:
Iran threatens action over oil routes if neighbouring countries supporting US in upping economic pressure on Tehran

Iran’s new top security chief has warned neighbouring countries against joining Washington’s campaign to squeeze Tehran’s economy, threatening retaliation and saying their interests could become targets.Mohsen Rezaei, the newly appointed head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council said Iran could target oil-shipping routes outside the Strait of Hormuz if neighbouring countries join what he described as an economic war against Tehran. Such countries would be considered enemies, he said, adding, “we will target their interests", as quoted by AP.His warning comes after US President Donald Trump vowed to impose an “unprecedented” level of economic warfare and isolation on Iran, which has faced sanctions for years.“If (Trump) wants to do something, we will retaliate in a seismic manner,” , Rezaei added in an interview with state broadcaster IRIB that aired Saturday.Rezaei also warned the US against sending additional military personnel to the region and accused Washington of increasing global nuclear insecurity. He said Iran would also make changes to its diplomacy and develop new capabilities for what he called the next war.The threats came as diplomatic efforts continued elsewhere. Egypt’s foreign minister discussed attempts to revive US-Iran negotiations with his Iranian counterpart, while Iraq and Iran said Tehran had facilitated the passage of some Iraqi oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.France and Saudi Arabia are also expected to discuss alternative routes around the waterway, while Israel carried out strikes in Syria and Gaza.
Article Summary: Mohsen Rezaei, the newly appointed head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council said Iran could target oil-shipping routes outside the Strait of Hormuz if neighbouring countries join what he described as an economic war against Tehran. Such countries would be considered enemies, he said.

Article Title: 'Conveyed our security concerns to US': Israel on Hamas disarmament plan
Article Text:
Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump (File photo)

Trump's proposed peace plan

Israel continues to strike Gaza

Israel has conveyed “serious security concerns” to the White House over the proposed disarmament deal with Hamas, an Israeli official said, in some of the first public comments from Israel since US President Donald Trump announced the agreement.According to Doror Spielman, a spokesperson for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office, Hamas remained “committed” to rebuilding its military rather than genuinely disarming. He stressed that the Israeli military would not withdraw from Gaza — where Tel Aviv currently controls more than 60% of the territory — until Hamas lays down its weapons.“Our assessment is that if we redeploy before Hamas is truly disarmed, it will quickly expand its presence throughout Gaza, rebuild its terrorist infrastructure, once again threaten Israeli communities, and seek to carry out another October 7-style attack,” Spielman told AP, referring to the Hamas militant attack on Israel in 2023 that triggered the war in the Gaza Strip.“Disarming means physically giving up the weapons. Nothing less,” he added.His remarks came days after Hamas announced that it would begin disarming as part of the US-brokered ceasefire agreement reached nine months ago to end the nearly three-year-long conflict. The development represents a potential breakthrough in efforts to end the war, although significant hurdles, conditions and lengthy timelines remain.Trump’s 20-point ceasefire plan requires Hamas to surrender its weapons and dismantle its tunnel network. It also envisions an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, a new technocratic Palestinian government, an international security force and the reconstruction of the devastated enclave.Under the agreement, weapons held by Hamas-run police would be transferred to the US-backed National Committee for the Administration of Gaza once it enters the enclave. The timing remains unclear, as it depends on other steps. Decommissioning and storing heavy weapons, along with dismantling military production sites and tunnels, would begin after the committee and international forces arrive and would coincide with a phased withdrawal.Areas under Tel Aviv's control have been largely destroyed and depopulated, while most of Gaza’s 2 million Palestinians remain in the rest of the territory, many in makeshift tent camps and damaged neighbourhoods.However, a significant withdrawal appears unlikely before Israel’s October elections. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces pressure from far-right coalition partners to maintain military operations and keep troops in Gaza, while opponents blame his government for failing to prevent the October 7, 2023, attack.Hamas-led militants killed about 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and abducted 251 others in the attack. Israel’s subsequent military campaign has killed more than 73,000 people, according to the Gaza health ministry.Meanwhile, Israel has continued striking Gaza since the ceasefire took effect last October, maintaining that its operations target Hamas and its infrastructure.At least 17 people, including children, were killed in the latest Israeli strikes, according to local hospitals. A strike on a residential apartment in southern Gaza killed three members of one family, including a 4-year-old child, according to Nasser Hospital.The Israeli military maintained that the strikes targeted militant operatives.
Article Summary: Israel has conveyed “serious security concerns” to the White House over the proposed disarmament deal with Hamas. Spokesman for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said Hamas remained ‘committed’ to rebuilding its military rather than disarming.

Article Title: Amid tensions with Pete Hegseth, US Army secretary Dan Driscoll to step down by year-end: Report
Article Text:
File photo: US army secretary Dan Driscoll (left) and US defence secretary Pete Hegseth (Picture credit: AP)

Driscoll's departure could leave Army without Senate-confirmed leader

Tensions with Hegseth

Focus on technology and Army modernisation

Trump had praised Driscoll

US Army secretary Dan Driscoll is expected to step down from his position by the end of 2026, or possibly earlier, following months of tension with US defence secretary Pete Hegseth, according to people familiar with the discussions cited by The Wall Street Journal.A separate report by The Hill also said Driscoll is looking to leave his role around the end of 2026. One source familiar with the discussions told the outlet that Driscoll has previously indicated that 23 to 24 months is the expected tenure of an Army secretary in the Trump administration.Driscoll's spokesperson declined to comment, while spokespeople for the Pentagon and Driscoll also declined to comment, according to the reports.Driscoll's departure would leave the Army without a Senate-confirmed secretary. The Army also currently does not have a Senate-confirmed chief of staff.Hegseth fired Gen Randy George as Army chief of staff in April without giving an explanation, and President Donald Trump has not nominated a permanent replacement.Gen Christopher LaNeve, the Army vice chief of staff and a former senior military aide to Hegseth, is serving as acting Army chief of staff.LaNeve has met with senators in recent months, but his confirmation is facing objections from lawmakers in both parties, according to The Hill.The developments would add to changes at senior levels of the Pentagon under Trump's second administration.Driscoll, a longtime friend and ally of Vice President JD Vance, has been involved in a simmering dispute over influence with Hegseth.According to The Wall Street Journal, tensions emerged early in the Trump administration after Driscoll offered to organise a visit by Vance and Trump to meet soldiers and discuss Army reforms.The tensions also flared after Trump selected Driscoll to negotiate with Ukrainian officials in an effort to help end the Russia-Ukraine war, according to The Hill.Driscoll and George had developed a close working relationship during Driscoll's tenure. Together, they pushed the Army to adopt new technologies and launched the Army Transformation Initiative, which focused on delivering warfighting capabilities, optimising force structure and eliminating waste and obsolete programmes.The initiative included efforts to integrate drones and artificial intelligence into Army formations.Driscoll also travelled to Ukraine with George and Gen Chris Donahue, then the Army's top general in Europe, to discuss peace negotiations with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.A former Army Ranger and venture capitalist, Driscoll has pushed the service to improve living conditions for soldiers, modernise equipment and draw lessons from Ukrainian forces on the use of commercial technology in warfare.During his tenure, private companies have pledged to invest more than $25 billion in data centres, critical mineral refineries and dining facilities on Army bases across the US.One source told The Hill that Driscoll had been “aggressive” in securing support from general officers for these initiatives because of his limited expected tenure.Driscoll's partnership with George ended after Hegseth removed the Army chief in April. The move drew criticism from Republican lawmakers and praise for George.During a congressional hearing, Driscoll called George “an amazing, transformation leader” when asked about his dismissal.Driscoll received praise from Trump at a defence conference in Pennsylvania last month.“With that beautiful smile, but he’s actually a killer. Look at that beautiful, nice, face. Everything’s so happy. He’s a killer. Would you believe it? Those are the best guys, actually,” Trump said.Driscoll was confirmed by the Senate on February 25, 2025, by a 66-28 vote.Trump had previously nominated Driscoll as Army secretary, describing him as a former soldier, investor and political adviser.Driscoll served with the US Army as a Cavalry Scout Platoon Leader with the 10th Mountain Division during Operation Iraqi Freedom before earning a law degree from Yale Law School.He later worked in venture capital and private equity and served as a senior adviser to Vance.
Article Summary: US Army secretary Dan Driscoll is expected to step down from his position by the end of 2026, or possibly earlier, following months of tension with US defence secretary Pete Hegseth. The Army also currently does not have a Senate-confirmed chief of staff. The developments would add to changes at senior levels of the Pentagon under Trump's second administration.

Article Title: Donald Trump shares image calling Hormuz 'new US territory'; Iran says strait 'closed'
Article Text:
​Trump, Iran clash over Hormuz as standoff over key waterway deepens

Image shared by Donald Trump (Image credit: Trump Truth Social)

US President Donald Trump on Sunday again shared an image on Truth Social describing the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz as “NEW US Territory”, even as Iran maintained that the waterway was closed and would remain so unless Washington changed its approach.Trump had first shared the same image on August 18. Speaking at a police academy on Long Island on August 14, he had said, “Pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Strait of Hormuz a territory of the United States.”Iran’s supreme national security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei, meanwhile, said Tehran would not reopen the strait unless the US fulfilled its commitments and changed its behaviour.“The Strait of Hormuz is closed and will not reopen,” Iran International quoted Rezaei saying. “If the United States changes its behavior and fulfills its commitments, the equation will be different, but this time the United States must act. It cannot be resolved through words and talks.”Despite Iran’s declaration, traffic through the waterway has increased in recent days. Nearly 200 ships crossed the Hormuz last week, compared with about 150 the previous week and around 40 two weeks earlier, according to UK maritime trade operations data cited by the New York Post.Maritime intelligence firm Kpler said more than 80% of liquid cargoes passing through the strait over the past two weeks either used an Omani route backed by the US and authorised by the International Maritime Organization, or went “dark”.Rezaei also said Iran had reached an agreement with Oman on a “middle route” through the strait, although a joint statement had yet to be finalised.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday again shared an image on Truth Social describing the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz as “NEW US Territory” Iran maintained that the waterway was closed and would remain so unless Washington changed its approach. Trump had first shared the same image on August 18.

Article Title: Ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan returns to Adiala Jail after medical examination at Islamabad hospital
Article Text:
73-year-old cricket legend facing health issues after 3 years of imprisonment

Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan on Friday returned to Rawalpindi's Adiala Jail shortly after undergoing a medical examination at Shifa Hospital in Islamabad.The development was confirmed to Reuters by a member of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.The 73-year-old cricket legend has been facing health issues after spending more than three years in prison following his tenure as prime minister.Khan was taken to Shifa Hospital days after the Supreme Court ordered a medical examination. An official from the Shehbaz Sharif-led government said Islamabad was complying with the Supreme Court's order to facilitate his medical examination.Khan's party and family had sought permission for him to remain in hospital.A three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination amid prolonged concerns raised by his family and personal doctors over his health and access to treatment.The court directed that a medical board, including specialists and his personal physician, Faisal Sultan, examine him.The Supreme Court's order came after former Pakistan president Arif Alvi shared Khan's vitals and raised concerns over what he described as "alarming" medical reports.In a post on X, Alvi said, "Imran Khan's medical reports are alarming. I have gone through them with several specialists, and I am writing this in plain language so every Pakistani can understand exactly what is happening."Alvi also highlighted Khan's health concerns, citing his "anxiety and stress levels", "palpitations," and "high blood pressure." He added that while sleeplessness was not mentioned in the report, Khan's medication appeared to suggest the problem.
Article Summary: Imran Khan returned to Adiala Jail after medical examination at Shifa Hospital in Islamabad. Khan, 73, has been facing health issues after spending more than three years in prison following his tenure as prime minister. A three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination.

Article Title: US debt crosses $40 trillion but everyone still trusts Uncle Sam. But for how long?
Article Text:
US national debt crossed $40 trillion, exceeding annual GDP, as interest payments approach $1 trillion, with economists warning of painful adjustments ahead.

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Amid The Urge To Splurge, Trump Has Proposed Hike Of 50% In Def Budget

Surprisingly, America is not mainly borrowing from China. The biggest lenders are actually Americans and American institutions – pension funds, mutual funds, banks, insurance companies, households and investment funds. Foreign governments and investors also buy what is euphemistically called “US Treasury securities”: Japan held about $1.12 trillion in June, Britain about $940 billion, China about $633 billion and India roughly $200 billion.

Yes, Uncle Sam, we’ll take your IOU.

The United States’ national debt crossed $40 trillion on Tuesday, a number so large that even breaking it up with commas can scarcely make it comprehensible. As in a 4 followed by 13 zeroes: $40,000,000,000,000!Number-crunching economists reached for various metrics to convey the scale of the crisis. The US economy produces roughly $33 trillion worth of goods and services a year. So the debt is now bigger than the entire annual economic output (GDP) of the country. Per American, that works out to roughly $118,000; for a family of four, about $472,000. Divvying it another way, the US is adding debt at a rate of roughly $90,000 every second.To put that in perspective for readers in India, the $40 trillion debt America has racked up is roughly 10 times the size of India’s entire annual economy. In other words — although debt versus GDP is not an apples-to-apples comparison — the US owes roughly ten times the value of everything India produces in a year. America’s debt mountain is therefore not merely bigger than India’s economy; it is about ten Indian economies stacked on top of one another.Economists also put the best possible spin by pointing out that the raw number itself is less important than debt relative to the size of the economy and the government’s ability to service it.Just the US debt held by its public is roughly equal to annual GDP, and the Congressional Budget Office says that, under current law, the ratio could rise to 120% of GDP by 2036 and 175% by 2056.So how did the world’s richest country get here? In the simplest terms, Washington has been spending more than it collects in taxes — year after year, administration after administration. Wars, tax cuts, the 2008 financial crisis, Covid stimulus, an ageing population and rising Social Security and Medicare costs have all added to the bill. The pandemic was particularly spectacular: debt exploded as the government tried to prevent an economic catastrophe.But the extraordinary thing is that America has continued borrowing heavily even after the emergencies have passed. Federal budget deficits are still running at levels normally associated with wars or recessions. The awkward question for Washington now is whether the borrowing eventually stops gently — or with a crash.So who is lending America $40 trillion?But why lend to a country this deeply in debt? Because US “Treasury securities” remain the world’s favourite financial equivalent of a steel safe with a very large lock. They are highly liquid, easily traded and backed by the world’s largest economy — as well as by Washington’s long-established record of paying its debts. In other words, America has been able to borrow on an extraordinary scale because the world keeps saying:For now.President Trump has repeatedly promised to reduce the national debt, including by using tariff revenue. But the arithmetic has not exactly been taking orders from the White House. Amid the irresistible American urge to splurge, Trump is proposing a $1.5 trillion military budget, roughly a 50% increase from recent levels and an unprecedented level of Pentagon spending, arguing that a stronger military is essential to national security.So America is essentially trying to lose weight while ordering a second dessert; spending like a drunken sailor on shore leave — and then promising the bartender that tariffs will somehow pay the tab.And debt is not merely about the amount borrowed. It is also about the interest bill. Interest payments are now approaching $1 trillion a year. That means an increasing share of the federal budget is going simply toward servicing yesterday’s borrowing rather than paying for today’s schools, roads, defence, healthcare or anything else Washington wants to spend money on.As the debt grows, investors could eventually demand higher interest rates to keep buying Treasury securities. That would feed through into mortgage rates, business borrowing costs and the government’s own financing costs, potentially slowing investment and economic growth. The US would then face the unpleasant menu economists have been warning about for years: higher taxes, slower spending, cuts to benefits, faster economic growth, inflation — or some combination of all of them.Washington would have to bring spending and revenues into better balance: restrain the growth of entitlement programmes, control discretionary spending, reconsider tax cuts, raise more revenue and — hardest of all — persuade voters that there is no painless option. There is no magic button marked “Pay Off $40 Trillion.”The CBO’s is essentially warning that the longer Washington waits, the more painful the eventual adjustment becomes. That is America’s peculiar fiscal paradox: the world’s richest country can afford an enormous debt — until one day the debt becomes so enormous that it starts deciding what the world’s richest country can afford. Or as one economist might put it, there is no such thing as a free lunch -- just a lunch somebody has put on the national credit card.
Article Summary: US national debt crossed $40 trillion, exceeding annual GDP, as interest payments approach $1 trillion, with economists warning of painful adjustments ahead. To put that in perspective for readers in India, the $40 trillions debt America has racked up is roughly 10 times the size of India’s entire annual economy.

Article Title: Japan installed a 1.1 MW turbine beneath the Naru Strait, using predictable tidal currents to generate clean electricity for the Goto Islands
Article Text:
Image AI generated

How Japan’s 1.1 MW AR1100 tidal turbine generates electricity underwater

Image AI generated

Japan’s tidal energy project grows from a 500 kW pilot to a 1.1 MW turbine

Why predictable tidal energy could complement solar and wind in Japan

The engineering challenges of operating a tidal turbine underwater

Between Japan’s Goto Islands, the sea is doing something that is usually associated with wind farms and solar fields. Beneath the surface of the Naru Strait, a 1.1 MW turbine is drawing energy from water moving with the tides and sending electricity back towards land through a subsea cable. No blades are turning in the sky and no panels spread across the shoreline. The machine works largely out of sight, following currents whose timing can be forecast well in advance. Installed by Proteus Marine Renewables, the AR1100 grew from an earlier 500 kW trial in the same waters. Its deployment has given Japan a megawatt-scale tidal system designed to work with the regular rise and fall of the sea rather than depending on sunshine or changing winds.The project also demonstrates the potential of tidal power in narrow channels, where fast-moving water can provide a concentrated source of renewable energy. By placing the turbine underwater, the system avoids taking up large areas of land while tapping into a resource that follows a predictable natural cycle.Unlike solar and wind power, tidal energy has one major advantage: its timing can be predicted years ahead because tides follow the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun.That predictability could make tidal turbines useful alongside renewable sources whose output changes with weather conditions.The AR1100 is installed in the Naru Strait near Japan’s Goto Islands. Unlike a conventional wind turbine, there is no tower standing above the water and no set of panels covering land. The generating equipment works underwater, where tidal currents pass through its three-bladed rotor and turn the machinery inside the nacelle. Electricity then travels towards shore through a subsea connection. According to Proteus Marine Renewables, the turbine was deployed in February 2025, while later company information recorded that it received Japanese certification and began exporting electricity to the grid in June 2025.The arrangement is fairly straightforward in principle, although operating it beneath the sea is not. The rotor extracts energy from moving water, the drivetrain passes that mechanical power to a permanent-magnet generator, and the resulting electricity is carried to an onshore station. A yaw system turns the nacelle as the tidal flow reverses, while independently controlled blades can alter their pitch to regulate how the turbine responds to changing conditions. AR1100 is a horizontal-axis turbine mounted on a gravity-based support structure. The earlier project in the same strait provided the starting point for the larger machine.Offshore Energy reported that the earlier 500 kW AR500 pilot operated in the Naru Strait with 97% availability in 2021. That earlier machine had a rated capacity of 500 kW and recorded 97% availability during its operation, according to the material released about the project. The experience allowed engineers to see how the technology behaved in the actual marine environment rather than only in controlled testing.The next version increased the rated capacity to 1.1 MW and introduced changes to the turbine's control systems. An equipment supply and works contract with Kyuden Mirai Energy was signed in November 2022, with the Japanese project subsequently moving towards the upgraded machine. Advanced pitch and yaw systems were incorporated as part of the work. The company says those changes were intended to improve the turbine's performance and efficiency while allowing it to deal more effectively with the changing direction of the tidal flow.The most distinctive feature of tidal power is not simply that the turbines sit underwater. It is the predictability of the resource. Solar output changes with daylight and weather conditions. Wind can strengthen, weaken or stop altogether. ClickPetroleogas noted that tidal production can be estimated in advance because the cycles follow predictable natural patterns, unlike renewable generation that is more affected by weather conditions. The electricity produced at any particular moment still depends on the conditions at the site and the performance of the equipment; the underlying movement of the water is far less of a surprise.That distinction matters when renewable sources are being combined. A grid operator cannot make the sun shine or order the wind to blow, whereas the timing of tidal cycles can be incorporated into generation planning. It does not make tidal energy constant; the flow rises and falls as the tide changes, but it makes the pattern easier to anticipate. For islands such as those around the Goto group, where space and fuel logistics can present particular constraints, a submerged source can sit alongside solar, wind and other forms of generation. The Naru Strait project is intended to contribute to reducing emissions from the islands' electricity supply.Underwater generation creates its own engineering problems. Components have to survive saltwater, strong currents and long periods of exposure while remaining accessible enough for inspection and maintenance. Getting people and equipment to a submerged turbine can also require vessels, specialist crews and careful planning. The location itself has to provide sufficient water movement, suitable depth and a practical route for sending the electricity into the grid.The Naru Strait project therefore depends on more than the turbine turning. Its subsea cable links the machine to an onshore electrical station, where the generated power can be processed for distribution. Local vessels and resources were used during deployment, with Proteus' offshore team overseeing the work, while Kyuden Mirai Energy and Japan's Ministry of Environment have been involved in advancing the project.There is also a useful way to think about the long-term promise of the machine, without treating its output as something that can be guaranteed hour by hour. The tidal timetable itself is highly predictable. Engineers can calculate when stronger and weaker currents are expected well into the future, creating a generation pattern that can be plotted ahead of time. What cannot simply be printed on that chart is the turbine's actual electricity production for every future hour: maintenance, operating conditions and other technical factors still matter.That distinction is important. The Naru Strait turbine is not a giant power station, nor does the available source material establish that it will produce a fixed amount of electricity every hour for a decade. What the project demonstrates is something more specific: a megawatt-scale machine can be installed beneath a Japanese strait, connected to shore and operated using an energy source whose basic timing is known far in advance. The water will keep changing direction. The turbine is built to follow it.
Article Summary: The AR1100 is installed in the Naru Strait near Japan’s Goto Islands. Unlike a conventional wind turbine, there is no tower standing above the water. The generating equipment works underwater, where tidal currents pass through its three-bladed rotor and turn the machinery inside the nacelle. Electricity then travels towards shore through a subsea connection.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Dwayne Johnson: "Be humble. Be hungry. And always be..." - a lesson on staying successful
Article Text:
Dwayne Johnson

Quote of the day by Dwayne Johnson

"Be humble. Be hungry. And always be the hardest worker in the room."

Dwayne Johnson’s success story is really about starting again

A simple way to actually use this idea

Other famous quotes by Dwayne Johnson

"Success isn't always about greatness. It's about consistency . Consistent hard work leads to success. Greatness will come."

. Consistent leads to success. Greatness will come." "If you have a dream, chase it. Because a dream doesn't work unless you do."

"The struggles along the way are only meant to shape you for your purpose."

Two people can reach a comparable level of success and carry themselves in completely different ways once they get there. One starts believing their own reputation, coasting on past results and expecting continued recognition without continued effort. The other keeps behaving, day to day, as though the position they've reached is still something to be earned rather than something already secured. Johnson, an actor and former professional wrestler who built one of the most consistently bankable careers in modern entertainment, has repeated some version of this line across interviews and public talks for years, treating it less as a motivational slogan and more as an operating discipline he applies to himself regardless of how much he's already accomplished. The three instructions build on each other deliberately: humility to keep success from distorting self-perception, hunger to keep ambition from going stale once a goal is reached, and outworking everyone else in the room as the concrete, checkable behaviour that proves the first two aren't just talk. His remarkable career trajectory proves that sustained success requires continuously earning respect through consistent effort, rather than simply resting on past achievements and accumulated reputation.What gives this line extra weight is how directly it maps onto Johnson's own well-documented history. Before wrestling or acting, he was cut from the Canadian Football League after a brief and unsuccessful professional football career, a setback that reportedly left him with only a few dollars to his name and forced him to move back in with his parents to rebuild from there. He then built a wrestling career from the ground up, working through years of small venues and modest paydays before becoming one of the most recognisable performers in WWE history.That same pattern repeated when he transitioned to acting, starting in supporting and low-budget roles before working his way, over roughly two decades, into becoming one of the highest-paid actors in the world. Johnson has spoken repeatedly about maintaining an intense personal work ethic, including famously early gym sessions and a demanding schedule, even at the peak of his commercial success, treating each new project as something that still has to be earned rather than something his existing fame should simply guarantee him.The useful move here is treating each of the three instructions as a separate check rather than a single vague attitude, since it's entirely possible to stay humble while quietly losing hunger, or to stay hungry while letting effort slide once recognition arrives. Humility alone can drift into complacency if nothing keeps pushing forward. Hunger alone can curdle into arrogance if nothing keeps it grounded. The third instruction, being the hardest worker in the room, is what actually forces the first two to remain honest rather than becoming things a person merely claims about themselves.A fair test, at any point success starts to feel comfortable, is to ask honestly whether the current level of effort would still hold up if nobody already knew your track record. That question won't manufacture motivation out of nothing. It usually reveals how much of the current effort is riding on reputation rather than on work still actually being done.
Article Summary: Dwayne Johnson is an actor and former professional wrestler. His quote of the day is about consistency and being the hardest worker in the room. Johnson has spoken repeatedly about maintaining an intense personal work ethic. He treats each new project as something that still has to be earned.

Article Title: 2-year-old dies after 'severe beating'; 18-year old mother, boyfriend arrested in Georgia
Article Text:
Georgia toddler’s death lands mother, boyfriend in custody

An 18 year old in Georgia has been arrested and charged after her boyfriend allegedly severely beat her 2-year-old son, who later died from his injuries.The Canton Police Department responded to a report of an unresponsive child at a residence on Cartersville Street at around 11.29 am (local time) on August 3, according to police.The child was taken to a local hospital, where he was later pronounced dead. In the days that followed, Canton police detectives interviewed 22-year-old Celso Edison Vicente Y Vicente, who was identified as the live-in boyfriend of the toddler’s 18-year-old mother, Devorah Diaz Perez.According to arrest warrants cited by local media, Vicente Y Vicente was responsible for caring for the child on the day of his death and allegedly struck and “severely beat” him with his hands and other unidentified objects. He was arrested around 7 pm (local time) that day and charged with malice murder and first-degree cruelty to children.He remains in custody at the Cherokee County Adult Detention Center, as cited by the People.More than two weeks after the toddler’s death, police also arrested Diaz Perez after detectives determined there was probable cause to charge her with second-degree murder, two counts of second-degree cruelty to children and three counts of reckless conduct.She was taken into custody and booked into the Cherokee County Adult Detention Center.“The death of a child is heartbreaking, and our thoughts are with everyone affected by this tragic loss,” Canton Police Chief Marty Ferrell was quoted as saying by the People.“Our detectives have worked diligently to conduct a thorough and professional investigation. We remain committed to protecting the integrity of this case and allowing the judicial process to move forward.”The Georgia Bureau of Investigation Medical Examiner’s Office will conduct an autopsy to determine the child’s official cause and manner of death.
Article Summary: Devorah Diaz Perez, 18, and Celso Edison Vicente Y Vicente, 22, are in custody. Vicente allegedly beat the 2-year-old boy with his hands and other unidentified objects. The toddler later died from his injuries.

Article Title: In 1881, a wealthy widow moved to California and kept expanding her home for 30 years; it became a 160-room maze with staircases to nowhere
Article Text:
Image(s): Winchester Mystery House

How the wealthy widow began the extraordinary building project in California

Sarah Winchester (Image: Wikipedia)

The 160-room mansion became a maze of doors and staircases

The mystery behind the mansion remains part of its legend

In 1881, Sarah Winchester became one of America’s wealthiest women after her husband, William Wirt Winchester, died and left her a vast inheritance. A few years later, the widow moved from Connecticut to California and bought an eight-room farmhouse in the Santa Clara Valley. What began as a modest renovation soon turned into an extraordinary building project that continued for 36 years, with rooms, corridors and architectural experiments added without a conventional master plan. By the time Winchester died in 1922, the house had grown into a sprawling Victorian mansion containing 160 rooms, thousands of windows and doors, and staircases that appeared to lead nowhere. Some stories claim she built endlessly to confuse restless spirits, while other explanations point to her fascination with architecture and desire to keep workers employed. Whatever motivated her, the result became one of California’s most unusual historic homes in America, drawing visitors intrigued by its strange rooms, hidden passages, elaborate craftsmanship and enduring mystery.Sarah Winchester’s transformation from wealthy widow to builder began after a loss. Her husband died in 1881, and she inherited a fortune tied to the Winchester rifle business. She eventually travelled west and settled near San Jose, purchasing an eight-room farmhouse in 1886.Rather than simply remodel it, she kept ordering new construction, creating a home that changed almost continuously. Carpenters worked without the benefit of a blueprint, allowing rooms and passages to appear wherever Winchester wanted them. According to Atlas Obscura, the project lasted 36 years and cost millions of dollars at the time. The expanding house became increasingly intricate, reflecting Winchester’s wealth, curiosity and willingness to experiment with unconventional architectural ideas throughout.The mansion’s strangest features are what made it famous. Staircases climb towards ceilings, doors open onto empty space, and some windows were placed inside rooms rather than facing outdoors. The completed building contained 160 rooms, 2,000 doors, 10,000 windows and dozens of stairways. Yet its oddities were mixed with modern comforts. The house had indoor plumbing, central heating and multiple elevators, showing that Winchester was not creating a chaotic curiosity. She also incorporated stained glass, decorative woodwork and other expensive details throughout the structure. Some architectural choices may have been practical experiments, while others remain difficult to explain. The result was less a conventional mansion than a changing maze, where domestic spaces could suddenly give way to a dead end.The famous explanation for the construction comes from a story about spiritualism. According to legend, a medium told Winchester that the spirits of people killed by Winchester rifles were seeking revenge and that she could avoid them by moving west and building continuously. Some versions claim she believed construction had to continue to prevent her death, while others say the confusing layout was intended to keep spirits lost inside the house. These claims remain part of the mansion’s mythology rather than established fact. Another possibility is less supernatural, Winchester may have enjoyed architecture, experimentation and the challenge of expanding her home. Whatever the truth, construction ended when she died in 1922, leaving a mansion whose design still invites speculation.
Article Summary: Sarah Winchester became one of America’s wealthiest women after her husband, William Wirt Winchester, died in 1881. A few years later, the widow moved from Connecticut to California and bought an eight-room farmhouse. What began as a modest renovation soon turned into an extraordinary building project that continued for 36 years. Some stories claim she built endlessly to confuse restless spirits, while other explanations point to her fascination with architecture and desire to keep workers employed.

Article Title: In 1920s Massachusetts, a divorcing couple agreed to build a duplicate house; the husband followed the deal but put the new home on an isolated salt marsh
Article Text:
Pink House at sunset (Image: Wikipedia)

Why the divorcing couple built this duplicate house on an isolated salt marsh

The house on the way to Plum Island (Image: Wikipedia)

The isolated salt-marsh house had a remarkably bleak reputation

New research challenged the famous spite-house legend

On Massachusetts’ Plum Island, a pale pink house once stood alone above the marsh, looking almost too picturesque for the strange story attached to it. Local legend claimed the unusual home was born from a bitter divorce in the 1920s. According to the tale, a wife demanded that her husband build an exact replica of their family home as part of their divorce agreement. He supposedly agreed, but found a loophole: she had never said where the new house had to be built. So the story goes that he recreated their home on an isolated salt marsh, turning an ordinary marital settlement into an act of revenge. The house even became known as a “spite house”. Yet historical research later cast doubt on much of the legend, revealing a more complicated story of separation, abandonment and an isolated family home that survived for decades.The story of the Pink House begins with a couple living in the Newbury area during the 1920s, a period when Plum Island was developing as a seasonal and year-round residential area. According to the long-running local tale, the couple were divorcing and their separation agreement required the husband to provide his wife with a house identical to the one they had shared. Rather than simply rebuild the home somewhere convenient, the husband supposedly interpreted the agreement literally.He built another house that matched the original but placed it in an extremely isolated location on Plum Island’s salt marsh. The detail that made the story so memorable was the alleged loophole. The wife had demanded a duplicate house, but, according to the legend, had failed to specify where it should be located. That supposedly allowed her husband to satisfy the agreement while making the new home as inconvenient as possible. The resulting building was eventually painted pink and became known as the Pink House. From a distance, its solitary position amid the marsh made it look almost dreamlike, but its reputation was considerably darker. Atlas Obscura describes the property as a rumoured spite house and notes that local lore has long portrayed it as a divorced husband’s final act of retaliation against his former wife.The location was central to the legend because the house stood far from the conveniences associated with ordinary domestic life. The story claims that the husband deliberately chose the remote marsh to make his former wife’s new home difficult to live in. One particularly striking detail concerns the plumbing. The Pink House reportedly used salt water rather than fresh water. That feature helped reinforce the idea that the building had been designed as a cruel joke rather than a genuine home. But that part of the story needs some qualification. The salt-water plumbing was not unusual on Plum Island during the 1920s because fresh running water was scarce or even unavailable in parts of the area. Indoor plumbing itself was also still relatively new in many American homes. In other words, a feature that later sounded like evidence of deliberate spite may actually have been typical of the island at the time. The house was not immediately abandoned, either. The family who built it reportedly used it as a summer home, despite owning other substantial properties in nearby Newburyport. After the house was sold in the 1940s, several other families lived there over the years. Eventually, however, the building became vacant. By the early 2000s, the Pink House had been left to weather the elements, standing alone against the marsh while birds of prey became its most frequent visitors. Hawks and snowy owls were among the species photographed around the abandoned building.For years, the story of the Pink House was repeated as a nearly perfect tale of divorce, revenge and an unfortunate loophole. But in 2017, a grassroots campaign called Support The Pink House carried out extensive research into the property's history and reached a less dramatic conclusion. Researchers found that the actual timeline did not neatly fit the popular story. The couple’s divorce occurred several years after they had moved into the house, although they separated relatively soon after moving in. The divorce documents also did not show a property being transferred as part of the settlement. More importantly, researchers could not find records proving that the original couple had lived in another house that the Pink House was designed to replicate. The evidence also weakened the claim that the house was deliberately made uninhabitable. Its family owners used it for years, while later families lived there as well.The spite-house label was uncertain, even while acknowledging that there was clearly plenty of personal bitterness surrounding the couple’s relationship. The legend nevertheless became inseparable from the building itself. Its lonely position, faded pink exterior and mysterious history transformed it into a beloved local landmark. For years, supporters campaigned to preserve it, hoping its unusual story would prevent it from disappearing. Those efforts ultimately failed. The Pink House was demolished by the US Fish and Wildlife Service , and it now records it as permanently closed. The site remains part of the Parker River National Wildlife Refuge, leaving the strange story of the lonely house behind even though the house itself is gone. What survives is not simply a tale of revenge. It is a reminder of how places gather stories around them, and how a house standing alone in a marsh can become more famous for the legend surrounding it than for the people who actually lived inside it.
Article Summary: Local legend claimed the unusual home was born from a bitter divorce in the 1920s. According to the tale, a wife demanded that her husband build an exact replica of their family home as part of their divorce agreement. He supposedly agreed, but found a loophole: she had never said where the new house had to be built. So the story goes that he recreated their home on an isolated salt marsh, turning an ordinary marital settlement into an act of revenge. Researchers found that the actual timeline did not neatly fit the popular story. The couple’s divorce occurred several years after they had moved into the house

Article Title: Flock CEO says privacy can't be the only priority; it is about safety, as Americans vandalize AI surveillance traffic cameras across US
Article Text:
Flock CEO defends his AI surveillance tool and says privacy can't be the only priority; it's about safety also.

What are Flock cameras?

Tracking but for the wrong reasons

Amid intense backlash over Flock surveillance cameras across America, Flock CEO Garrett Langeley told Fox News that privacy is not the only priority. “I think these are important conversations to have,” he told Saturday in America co-host Kayleigh McEnany, after she asked about the privacy concerns. “I value my privacy… but what we’re talking about is safety as well. And so I think when people talk about just one of these things, privacy or safety, they’re prioritizing the wrong thing. What we have to prioritize as a country is compromise: how do we have our safety, and how do we balance privacy?”Langeley said the call to ban the technology is absurd but there should be regulations. “That’s like banning vehicles. That would never have made sense,” Langley said about a ban. “Instead what we did is we introduced laws against drunk driving, laws around airbags.”It is a surveillance camera system that records and analyses everything that comes in front of it. The company sells its services as a crime-fighting tool and some law enforcement agencies have contracts with Flock to use the cameras' automated license plate readers.Flock has 120,000 automated license plate readers and pan-tilt-zoom cameras throughout the US, which capture billions of data points each month.Flock's ALPRs automatically scan the license plates that pass them, while PTZs record live footage that can be reviewed and analyzed.Flock has been making headlines for all the wrong reasons and police has been caught using the system to stalk exes and colleagues, though the company claimed that the cameras can't track people and they can only log vehicles.Dozens of Flock cameras have been forcibly destroyed in recent weeks. In June, a West Virginia man accused of destroying several Flock cameras was arrested.At least 56 municipalities have deactivated, canceled or rejected contracts with Flock this year, according to national advocacy organization DeFlock. The company announced changes aimed at addressing concerns about privacy and misuse. Flock introduced updated policies around auditing, as well as data retention and sharing – although many critics calling for change consider them inadequate.
Article Summary: Flock has 120,000 automated license plate readers and pan-tilt-zoom cameras throughout the US, which capture billions of data points each month. The company sells its services as a crime-fighting tool and some law enforcement agencies have contracts with Flock.

Article Title: 'Never': Indian-origin doctor denies assault allegations from students after arrest at Miami International Airport, released on bond
Article Text:
Dr Ranjith Ramasamy, a former Miami doctor, denied sexual assualt allegations and said he voluntarily returned from Dubai to clear his name.

Arrest warrant was issued against him in 2025

Ramasamy says disgruntled members are behind allegations

Dr Ranjith Ramasamy, an award-winning urologist who was arrested last week at Miami International Airport on charges of sexually assaulting his students, said he never sexually assaulted anyone. Ramasamy also said that he voluntarily came back to the US from Dubai, where he had been working lately, after the false accusations came as he wanted to clear his name.The 45-year-old urologist was handcuffed at the airport on his arrival at 10.45 pm on August 20. He appeared in court that afternoon and walked out on a $120,000 bond. Dr Ramasamy has been placed on house arrest. According to a Miami Herald report, Dr Ramasamy will be staying with his wife and children at a home in Sarasota. Court records mentioned that he surrendered after returning from Dubai.Dr Ramasamy was employed at the University of Miami as a professor of urology and director of male reproductive medicine and surgery. An arrest warrant was issued against him in October 2025 after he was charged with three counts of sexual battery,Three of Ramasamy's students, whom the doctor allegedly diagnosed with different conditions, told detectives that Ramasamy performed prostate exams that were "much longer and aggressive" than regular prostate exams.“None of these procedures were medically indicated, they were performed in a manner inconsistent with the standard of care, alone and after normal business hours, and fall far outside the acceptable bounds of any medical practice,” detectives said in the warrant after speaking to another three victims.Dr Ramasamy said the slanderous allegations against him came from "disgruntled members of the university community". He said he wanted to address the accusations, but the university did not provide him with records. He said he moved to Dubai in 2024 before the criminal charges were brought and he left his university in good standing and his license to practice in Florida remained active."I never performed any unnecessary medical procedure. I never assaulted anyone. I never sexually assaulted anyone, never," Ramasamy said.
Article Summary: Dr Ranjith Ramasamy, 45, was arrested at Miami International Airport on August 20. He was charged with three counts of sexual battery against three of his students. He said the slanderous allegations against him came from "disgruntled members of the university community" He has been placed on house arrest.

Article Title: Trump drops 2 names to replace Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary
Article Text:
Trump added that Leavitt would remain involved as one of his “top outside advisors”

US President Donald Trump on Friday named two people, commentor Scott Jennings and White House communications adviser Margo Martin, as potential contenders to succeed Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary, weeks before her planned departure.Asked who could replace Leavitt, Trump singled out Jennings, saying, “Scott Jennings is good,” before pointing to Martin and asking reporters, “Maybe Margo? What do you think of Margo?”Trump also mentioned an unnamed female supporter from Iowa as a possible choice and jokingly suggested NewsNation correspondent Kellie Meyer could take the role.The president praised Leavitt's tenure and said the position had become particularly attractive under her leadership.“I have never had so many job applications in my entire life. They all want that job. They love that job,” Trump told reporters while travelling to South Carolina.Leavitt, who became the youngest White House press secretary when she took office at 27 in January 2025, is set to leave the post at the end of August to spend more time with her two young children and family. Trump announced her decision on August 12, saying he “totally understand[s] and respect[s]” it.Jennings, a prominent CNN commentator and frequent defender of the Trump administration, previously served as a special assistant to President George W. Bush and as an adviser to Republican Senator Mitch McConnell.Martin serves as a special assistant to Trump and communications adviser at the White House. Trump did not indicate that either Jennings or Martin had been formally selected, and the White House has yet to announce Leavitt's successor.Jennings was also the leading contender on prediction market Kalshi on Friday, with a 41% probability of being chosen, followed by deputy press secretary Anna Kelly at 19%.Leavitt is expected to make her final official trip as Trump's press secretary on Saturday, when she accompanies him to Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, for a rally supporting Republican Senate candidate Darline Graham. She is expected to remain in Trump's political orbit after leaving the podium, taking up a senior advisory role at his MAGA Inc. super PAC.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday named two people, commentor Scott Jennings and White House communications adviser Margo Martin, as potential contenders to succeed Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary. Trump also mentioned an unnamed female supporter from Iowa as a possible choice and jokingly suggested NewsNation correspondent Kellie Meyer could take the role. Trump did not indicate that either Jennings or Martin had been formally selected.

Article Title: Gujarati man sentenced to 9 years in jail in US for scam; attorney says he grew up in India in extreme poverty without water, studied only till 10th
Article Text:
Gujarati man sentenced to 9 years in prison for financial fraud targeting elderly people.

Unpacking the massive scam targeting the elderly

Raval led investigators to Al Capone aka Shreyas Baldevbhai Chaudhary

Born in extreme poverty, slept on a mattress

A Gujarati fraudster who was arrested in 2024 by the FBI for a massive elderly scam was sentenced to nine years in prison by US district court in Cleveland. Judge J Philip Calabrese sentenced Shreyas Baldevbhai Chaudhary to 110 months in prison -- 9 years and two months in prison -- and his aide Trusha Chaudhary five years of probation.Shreyas was ordered to pay restitution of $5,164,031, and Trusha was ordered to pay $343,641.A third person in the operation Nitinkumar Raval was sentenced to 19 to 41 months in federal prison last December. He was also ordered to pay restitution of $224,902.In October 2023, a man from Salem, Massachusetts, clicked on a pop-up ad and his computer was frozen with a message that asked him to contact the Microsoft security phone number provided. He called the number and spoke to someone named Howard who put the man in touch with Stacy Brown. Brown told the man that he was a victim of identity theft and had to send $11,000 worth of gift cards.It was just the beginning. Next, Brown told the man to withdraw about $61,000 and send it to them following their instructions and arrangement. The next order was to withdraw $50,000 from his bank. This was when the bank suspected something was wrong and alerted the FBI.On a given date, when a courier (Raval) came to pick up the money, the FBI took him into custody and learned that a man named 'Al Capone' had instructed him to pick up the package.Investigators unmasked the 'Al Capone' as Shreyas who acted as director of couriers of US currency and property and directed the couriers to travel to various locations in the US to collect money from victims.The scam went on from December 2022 to December 2023.Shreyas's attorney pleaded for a lighter sentence and cited his childhood poverty in India. "Mr Chaudary was born and raised in the rural neighborhood of Ampura, in the state of Gujarat, India. He grew up in extreme poverty -- water was scarce, his house was in poor condition, and he slept on a mattress on the floor," the filing said."Mr Chaudhary only has a 10th-grade education and speaks very little English. Mr Chaudhary obtained his first job at twenty-two years of age and earned only $10.49 per month," it stated adding that Shreyas did not dispute the illegality of his behavior but prayed to the court to consider how life of extreme poverty would contribute to his decision to commit a financial crime.
Article Summary: Gujarati man sentenced to 9 years in prison for financial fraud targeting elderly people. Judge J Philip Calabrese sentenced Shreyas Baldevbhai Chaudhary to 110 months in prison. A third person in the operation Nitinkumar Raval was sentenced to 19 to 41 months in federal prison last December.

Article Title: In 1974, the National Park Service bought the Stewart family's 890-acre California ranch; they negotiated the right to remain and continued ranching there until 2021
Article Text:
Photo credit: Canva (Representative image)

Deep roots along the Northern California coast

The buyout and the life estate

The reality of working inside a national seashore

A lasting blueprint for

public and private cooperation

When the federal government stepped in to buy the Stewart family's 890-acre ranch in 1974, most people assumed a century of family cattle operations had reached its end. The acquisition was part of a major initiative to build out California's Point Reyes National Seashore, setting up an obvious conflict between public land preservation and private agricultural traditions. But the result was unexpected, according to official records from the National Park Service (NPS). Instead of vacating their generational homestead, the Stewarts negotiated a unique life estate agreement. This deal granted them the legal right to stay on the property and run their working ranch for nearly five additional decades. By the time the family officially retired in 2021, closing out roughly 150 years of continuous stewardship, they had demonstrated how agricultural heritage and modern park management can successfully coexist on public land.Long before government planners mapped out Point Reyes as a national park, the Stewart family was busy building a life along the rugged California coastline. Their ancestors originally arrived on the peninsula during the mid-19th century, clearing pastures, establishing homestead buildings, and introducing livestock to the coastal climate. In the decades that followed, the operation became a foundation for the region’s agricultural economy.Ranching in this coastal locale demanded constant effort and a deep understanding of weather, soil, and vegetation. For generations, the family regarded the land as more than a commercial asset or a place of work: it was a living legacy that required daily care and careful stewardship.By the early 1970s, shifting national priorities around land preservation brought the federal government right to the family's front gate. The National Park Service was actively securing acreage across the peninsula to safeguard its natural ecosystems and scenic views from commercial development. Many nearby landholders sold their properties and moved elsewhere, assuming that federal ownership automatically meant the end of private farming. The Stewarts took a different approach during negotiations. They understood that the agency wanted to protect the coastal environment, but they argued that working farmers could actually help maintain those open spaces.Their negotiation produced a life estate agreement, a rare legal arrangement allowing the family to live on the land and continue raising cattle while title ownership transferred to the public domain.Operating a working cattle ranch inside a high-visibility national park came with constant responsibilities. For nearly fifty years after the agreement, the Stewarts had to adapt their daily operations to meet strict environmental protections. Living next to protected coastal environments required the family to think carefully about how and when to graze cattle so as not to damage native flora or overgraze the land. The family was careful to monitor water sources, prevent soil erosion in local creeks, and work directly with park rangers and environmental specialists to schedule chores. These rules were not considered as a hindrance but rather became part of the Stewarts’ routine, showing the reality that responsible cattle management can be an active part of the local ecological health. Adapting to modern pressures and public interest As the decades went by, the environment surrounding the ranch changed dramatically. California’s population swelled, tourism on the coast burgeoned and millions of people began passing through Point Reyes every year to check out the beaches and hiking trails. Ranch life was no longer hidden away; it was happening right before the eyes of curious tourists and outdoor lovers. The Stewarts embraced this change by reaching out to the public. They talked with hikers, hosted school groups and helped visitors learn about West Marin’s agricultural history. Meanwhile, environmental laws kept changing, meaning the ranch had to keep updating its facilities.The family consistently found practical ways to modernize their work while preserving the traditional character of the landscape.In 2021, after nearly a century and a half of continuous stewardship, the Stewart family decided it was time to step back from the heavy physical demands of daily ranching. Their retirement marked the close of a historic chapter for Point Reyes, but their physical and operational footprint remains visible throughout the seashore.Visitors to the park today can still walk past the historic barns, wooden fences, and rolling pastures that fed generations of cattle. Interpretive displays tell the story of the family’s unusual pact with federal regulators, proving private citizens and government agencies can work together toward shared goals. The Stewart ranch remains a potent symbol for today’s conservationists, showing that preserving natural landscapes doesn’t mean erasing the human history and traditions that created them.
Article Summary: The Stewart family's 890-acre ranch in Northern California was bought by the National Park Service in 1974. Instead of vacating their generational homestead, the Stewarts negotiated a unique life estate agreement. This deal granted them the legal right to stay on the property and run their working ranch for nearly five additional decades. The family retired in 2021, closing out roughly 150 years of continuous stewardship.

Article Title: ‘Pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot’: Trump's appeal to voters ahead of midterms
Article Text:
Trump also urged his supporters to carry that approach into other elections, making clear that his backing of Graham was part of a broader effort to strengthen Republican support.

Trump backs Graham despite debate stumble

Graham leans into outsider image

Runoff tests Trump's influence

US President Donald Trump on Friday urged South Carolina Republicans to “pretend” he was on the ballot and turn out to vote for Darline Graham in Tuesday’s Senate runoff, using his own political popularity to rally support for the Republican political newcomer.Speaking at a campaign rally in Myrtle Beach, Trump said Republican candidates often struggle to attract the same turnout when he himself is not contesting an election, and urged his supporters to treat the Senate race as though his name appeared on the ballot.“The problem that we have is, they say that Trump does great when he’s on the ballot, but when he’s not on the ballot, his people don’t come and they don’t vote for senators, congressmen and other Republicans,” Trump said.“So what I really want you to do is pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot. Just come and vote. It’s so important,” he said.Trump also urged his supporters to carry that approach into other elections, making clear that his backing of Graham was part of a broader effort to strengthen Republican support.“We have to get Darline and other people elected.”Trump's appeal came as Graham faces Republican US Representative Ralph Norman in Tuesday's runoff to determine the party's candidate for the Senate seat left vacant by the death of her brother, veteran Senator Lindsey Graham, in July.Trump swiftly endorsed Darline Graham after her brother's death and has now made her campaign a test of his influence with Republican voters.The political novice faces criticism over her limited experience in foreign policy, particularly after a stumble during Tuesday's debate. Asked about the US alliance with Taiwan, Graham openly acknowledged that national security was not her area of expertise."I'm just going to be honest here. I'm not that informed on national ​security," she said. "National security is not my thing."Trump defended her response on Friday, calling it a “very honest answer” and saying she would follow the priorities of the military and the president."She's going to do what the military wants, ​and, really, what the president ​wants."Graham, whose career before politics focused on services for people with disabilities, has embraced criticism that she is not a conventional politician."The critics say I shouldn't run for the Senate," Graham said. "They say I'm not a politician. You know ​what I say? Guilty as charged."Her campaign has focused largely on domestic conservative issues, including restricting transgender rights, supporting Trump's immigration agenda and opposing abortion access.Trump contrasted her political focus with that of her late brother, saying Lindsey Graham was “very much about the world”, while Darline Graham was “more about affordability”.Graham and Norman emerged from a 10-candidate Republican field on August 11, with Graham securing 32.8% of the vote and Norman 24.6%. Neither won the majority needed to avoid a runoff.The contest has since centred heavily on which candidate is more closely aligned with Trump, with both seeking to present themselves as loyal supporters of the president.“Darline Graham supports President Donald J. Trump every day on every major issue,” South Carolina Republican Senator Tim Scott said at the rally.Trump's intervention also comes as Republicans prepare for the November midterm elections, when control of Congress will be at stake. By urging voters to imagine that he is personally on the ballot, Trump is seeking to turn his own political following into turnout for Republican candidates beyond his presidency.The president's influence is likely to be closely watched in the race, even though South Carolina remains a Republican stronghold. Trump won the state by 18 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election.Trump has previously used a very different tone when Democratic candidates have struggled with foreign policy questions. In February, he sharply criticised Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez after she stumbled over a Taiwan-related question.“Her performance was horrible. I was surprised actually, I didn’t know she was stupid."
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump urged South Carolina Republicans to “pretend” he was on the ballot and turn out to vote for Darline Graham in Tuesday’s Senate runoff. Graham faces Republican US Representative Ralph Norman in Tuesday's runoff to determine the party's candidate for the Senate seat left vacant by her brother, veteran Senator Lindsey Graham, in July.

Article Title: Over 700 US troops killed, wounded as Iran war nears seventh month
Article Text:
(Representative image) The Pentagon has also reportedly been slow to disclose information about wounded service members, citing security concerns (Photo: AP).

Up to 774 US service members have reportedly been killed or wounded as the US-Iran conflict approaches its seventh month, according to recent casualty figures released by the Pentagon.The figures, reported by The Washington Post based on the Pentagon’s casualty reporting system, include 18 deaths and 756 wounded service members.Data from the Defence Casualty Analysis System (DCAS), dated August 21, lists up to 14 deaths and 417 wounded under “Operation Epic Fury”. When figures listed under a separate “Overseas Operations” category are included, the reported death toll rises to 18.According to CNN, the Pentagon created the “Overseas Operations” category in DCAS last month to record service members killed or wounded “starting July 7”. The date coincided with the Trump administration informing Congress that a new conflict with Iran had begun.The Pentagon has not specified which conflict is covered by the category and has faced scrutiny over changes to its casualty data.The Washington Post reported that the Pentagon recently added a significant number of troops to its wounded list even as a fragile ceasefire largely remained in place. However, some of the increase could be linked to delays between injuries being recorded in the military’s medical system and appearing in the Pentagon’s database.The casualty figures have also fluctuated as Iranian attacks continued. CNN reported that four deaths and dozens of injuries temporarily disappeared from the database before being restored. The US Department of War attributed the changes to “temporary data disruptions”.The Pentagon has also reportedly been slow to disclose information about wounded service members, citing security concerns.Despite the scale of the reported casualties, neither side has resumed large-scale combat operations. US President Donald Trump did not extend the ceasefire after it expired on Monday.On Wednesday, Trump said the situation with Iran was “so good”, even as negotiations between Washington and Tehran remained paused. Control of the Strait of Hormuz also remains a key point of contention in the conflict.
Article Summary: Up to 774 US service members have reportedly been killed or wounded as the US- Iran conflict approaches its seventh month. The figures, reported by The Washington Post based on the Pentagon’s casualty reporting system, include 18 deaths and 756 wounded service members. Despite the scale of the reported casualties, neither side has resumed large-scale combat operations.

Article Title: US Death Valley tragedy: French tourist dies after vehicle gets stuck in 47°C heat
Article Text:
US Death Valley National Park. Photo credit: AP
